Rashid’s expression does not soften. “It’s a reasonable choice. It doesn’t make the term less ugly.”

“A contract can be ugly and enforceable,” Ashara says. “Those are different problems.”

Thessaly considers this. “If you weren’t permitted to know the library’s name, you weren’t given much way to complain about it afterward. That was likely deliberate.”

Caelindra reaches for the bread basket. “A library that hides its own name sounds exhausting.”

“It was a job,” Rashid says. “Not a courtship.”

“That does not make obscurity charming.”

A server replaces the empty soup bowls with plates of peppered roast and glazed roots. Aldric waits until the server has moved away before speaking.

“The Academy keeps counsel for Conclave students. They may not be able to undo an outside agreement, but they can tell you what it requires of you here.” He looks at you steadily. “Do you still have a copy of the contract?”
